blurb: A `\u{…}` escape must name a Unicode scalar value, so a string is always valid text. A surrogate (`D800` to `DFFF`) is half of a UTF-16 pair and stands for no character on its own, and anything above `10FFFF` is outside Unicode. Write the code point of the character you mean, such as `\u{E9}` for `é`. A `\u` with no braces, no digits or more than six digits is `bynk.lex.bad_escape`.
example:
const Mark: String = "\u{D800}"    // ✗ a surrogate is not a character
const Mark: String = "\u{E9}"      // ✓ `é`
summary: A `\u{…}` escape names a surrogate or a value above U+10FFFF.
